headline_findings: Deny-first fixed precedence (Claude, Codex profiles) vs last-match-wins (opencode) vs model-graded safety (Cline, Cursor classifier) are the three permission design poles in 2026.
Native Windows command sandboxing is the industry-wide hole: only experimental AppContainer/Integrity-Level approaches exist; Claude and Cursor defer to WSL2.
Approval UX converges on once/session/always/deny plus diff or command preview; Cline's shadow-git checkpoints are the most forgiving undo model.
Classifier auto-review modes (Claude auto, Codex auto-review, Cursor Auto-review) cut prompt fatigue but vendors state they are non-boundaries.
Auditability is hook/transcript JSONL based; hash-chained logs, rotation, redaction and fail-closed policy are cheap patterns Cerebro can copy.

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent fit: pure host-side JSON rules, zero GPU/RAM cost; PowerShell rule support matters on Win11; pair with WSL2 or job-object limits.
items.harness_integration: Copy deny-first precedence and Tool(specifier) glob syntax into Cerebro config; enforce in Rust before spawning llama.cpp argv; add /permissions-style TUI list.
items.name: Claude Code allow/ask/deny rules with modes
items.quality_cost: None on model quality; misordered rules silently over/under-permit, and prefix Bash matches are bypassable by path or sh -c.
items.what: Three rule lists (allow, ask, deny) with deny-then-ask-then-allow precedence plus modes: manual, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions.
items.where_implemented: Claude Code settings.json permissions.allow/ask/deny, permissions.defaultMode, /permissions dialog

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent fit: hooks are local scripts with timeouts; keep allowlist of interpreters (powershell.exe, node) and short timeouts on laptop.
items.harness_integration: Add PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook Bicameral hook bus in Rust: spawn hook exe with JSON on stdin, honor allow/deny/ask JSON plus exit-2-blocks semantics.
items.name: Claude Code PreToolUse hook policy gate
items.quality_cost: None; risk is silent failure (hooks not firing on Windows, ask ignored under auto mode) leaving users unprotected.
items.what: User scripts run before/after each tool call and can allow, deny, prompt, or rewrite tool input; the community audit-log mechanism.
items.where_implemented: Claude Code hooks PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied in settings.json

items.fit_reference_machine: Partial fit: no native Windows sandbox, so on this laptop it only helps inside WSL2; document which path each benchmark used.
items.harness_integration: Approximate with Windows job objects plus integrity levels for the llama.cpp child, and deny rules as the text layer on top.
items.name: Claude Code Bash sandbox auto-allow
items.quality_cost: None observed; sandboxed commands that need full access fall back to prompts or classifier.
items.what: Built-in Bash sandbox on macOS, Linux and WSL2 lets allowlisted-shape commands run with auto-allow while deny/ask rules still apply.
items.where_implemented: Claude Code sandbox.enabled and autoAllowBashIfSandboxed settings, /sandbox command

items.fit_reference_machine: Good fit conceptually; on native Win11 use read-only default plus on-request approvals since the Windows sandbox is experimental.
items.harness_integration: Mirror the two-axis model: sandbox mode gates what the llama.cpp child and tool scripts can touch; approval policy gates when the TUI prompts.
items.name: Codex sandbox modes x approval policies
items.quality_cost: Stricter modes add prompts, not quality loss; YOLO-equivalent danger-full-access removes all gates.
items.what: Sandbox mode (read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access) crossed with approval policy (on-request, never, unless-trusted, on-failure, granular).
items.where_implemented: Codex CLI config.toml sandbox_mode and approval_policy, --sandbox and --ask-for-approval flags

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent fit: static prefix rules cost nothing at runtime and suit a small office sharing .codex/execpolicy files.
items.harness_integration: Implement prefix_rule-style allow/prompt/forbidden lists for shell tools in Cerebro config; session accept persists a rule like Codex does.
items.name: Codex execpolicy Starlark rules
items.quality_cost: Overly broad patterns silently erase the approval boundary; docs advise narrow prefixes like cargo test over python.
items.what: Starlark prefix_rule entries with allow, prompt or forbidden decisions persist trusted commands per project and across sessions.
items.where_implemented: Codex .codex/execpolicy/*.rules files plus accept-and-add-to-policy approval UI

items.fit_reference_machine: Good fit when stable; filesystem read/write/deny plus .env carve-outs map well to a small office least-privilege setup on Win11.
items.harness_integration: Adopt profile schema (named profiles, extends, workspace roots, .env deny globs, domain allow/deny) as Cerebro permission profiles v1.
items.name: Codex permission profiles (beta)
items.what: Named profiles combining filesystem read/write/deny rules with network domain policy enforced through a proxy feature.

items.fit_reference_machine: Poor direct fit: needs a second reviewer model, doubling VRAM/RAM pressure on an 8GB Ampere card at batch 1; use tiny local gate instead.
items.harness_integration: Approximate with a deterministic rule gate plus optional small-model review step that can be disabled on the reference laptop.
items.name: Codex and Cursor classifier auto-review
items.quality_cost: Non-deterministic both directions: can allow what a user would block and vice versa; vendors say it is not a security boundary.
items.what: A separate reviewer/classifier agent decides sandbox-escalation approvals instead of prompting the user; grants no new access.
items.where_implemented: Codex approvals_reviewer=auto_review; Cursor Auto-review mode on Claude 4.5 Haiku or GPT-5.4 Mini

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent fit: trivial CPU cost, single JSON file, per-agent overlays suit coding-agent vs chat-agent splits on a laptop.
items.harness_integration: Adopt per-tool glob objects plus external_directory guard; but choose deny-first instead of last-wins, and default to ask, not allow.
items.name: opencode permission map with last-match-wins
items.quality_cost: Permissive defaults plus last-wins ordering risk silent over-permission; .env deny default is the main safe built-in.
items.what: Allow/ask/deny map keyed by tool with glob per-pattern objects where the last matching rule wins; --auto flips asks to approvals.
items.where_implemented: opencode opencode.json permission key, --auto flag, v2 ordered permissions array with action/resource/effect

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent fit for a small office: global deny that repos cannot lift maps to owner-managed Cerebro policy on shared machines.
items.harness_integration: Add a binary org-policy layer above per-agent rules: broader-scope deny wins, allow only lifts earlier deny, never prompts.
items.name: opencode per-agent rules plus org policies
items.quality_cost: None; policies only ever tighten what permissions would otherwise allow.
items.what: Agent-specific permission overlays appended after global rules, plus binary experimental policies where broader authority always wins.
items.where_implemented: opencode agents.<id>.permissions and experimental.policies with permission:<action>:<resource> statements

items.fit_reference_machine: Good fit for friction, risky for safety: zero config cost but model-graded safety is non-deterministic on any hardware.
items.harness_integration: Do not copy model-graded safety; if used, restrict to read-only classification and keep destructive commands on explicit rules.
items.name: Cline category auto-approve with model-graded commands
items.quality_cost: Model marks each command requires_approval itself; docs say examples are not guarantees, so risky commands can slip through.
items.what: Per-category toggles (read/edit project/all files, safe/all commands, browser, MCP) where the model flags commands safe or approval-required.
items.where_implemented: Cline Auto Approve settings, yoloModeToggled, SDK toolPolicies autoApprove flags

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent fit: shadow git snapshots cost disk, not VRAM; ideal safety net for an offline laptop harness with destructive tools.
items.harness_integration: Snapshot workspace (git-based shadow repo) after each tool call; offer per-step Compare diff plus restore-files/task/both in the TUI.
items.name: Cline checkpoints with Compare and Restore
items.quality_cost: None on quality; restores can desync conversation context from files if only one side is rolled back.
items.what: Shadow-git snapshot after every tool call with multi-file diff Compare and Restore of files, task messages, or both.
items.where_implemented: Cline CheckpointTracker and TaskCheckpointManager, checkpoint Compare/Restore buttons, /undo in CLI

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent fit: folder trust plus safe mode directly suits consultants opening untrusted client repos on one laptop.
items.harness_integration: Add workspace trust: untrusted folders ignore project policy, disable auto-approve modes, skip MCP/env loading until user trusts.
items.name: Gemini trusted folders with safe mode
items.quality_cost: None; untrusted mode only restricts config loading and forces prompts.
items.what: Per-folder trust decision gating project settings, .env, extensions and MCP; untrusted folders force prompt-everything safe mode.

items.fit_reference_machine: Good fit: TOML policy plus expansion dialogs are cheap; Docker-based sandbox works on Win11 where native options are weakest.
items.harness_integration: Copy the policy-engine shape (tool, decision, priority, modes, argsPattern) and turn sandbox denials into scoped one-run approval dialogs.
items.name: Gemini policy engine plus sandbox expansion
items.quality_cost: None; expansion approvals are per-run and scoped to the denied paths or network.
items.what: TOML policy rules per tool and mode plus sandbox-expansion dialogs that convert a denial into a scoped one-run permission grant.
items.where_implemented: Gemini CLI ~/.gemini/policies/*.toml, plan.toml tiers, Sandbox Expansion Request modal

items.fit_reference_machine: Mixed fit: Seatbelt/Landlock help macOS/Linux, but on Win11 only WSL2 is supported, so native-laptop tests must note the sandbox gap.
items.harness_integration: Offer Docker-based tool sandboxing as the Windows story (like Gemini) instead of pretending prefix rules contain anything.
items.name: Windows sandbox gap across harnesses
items.quality_cost: Sandboxed commands needing full access fail or reroute to prompts; behavior differs between native and WSL2 runs.
items.what: Only experimental native Windows enforcement exists (Codex AppContainer token, Gemini icacls integrity); others require WSL2 or Docker.
items.where_implemented: Codex elevated/unelevated Windows sandbox; Gemini windows-native; Cursor WSL2-only; agentguard run refuses on Windows

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent fit: three shipped patterns (JSONL log, hash chain, rotation/redaction) are all offline and laptop-cheap.
items.harness_integration: Log every tool call as hash-chained JSONL from a separate process; add report/tail commands and fail-closed policy like cc-audit.
items.name: Community audit-log hooks (cc-audit, agentguard, PolicyApprovalGate)
items.quality_cost: None; fail-open internals keep a crashing auditor from bricking sessions while fail-closed policy keeps defaults enforced.
items.what: Local-only PreToolUse auditors writing append-only JSONL with blocklists, hash chains, rotation, redaction and session reports.
items.where_implemented: cc-audit audit-policy.yaml; agentguard hook plus dashboard; policygate install-hook --host claude|codex
